title: Gabber–Ramero obstruction ideal from a finite polynomial presentation
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $B$ a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. A finite polynomial presentation means a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism $\pi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$, with $n\geq0$ and $L=\ker\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $M=L/L^2$, the quotient module [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module], with $B$-action $b[f]=[pf]$ for any $p\in P$ with $\pi(p)=b$. Here $L^2$ is the ideal of finite sums of products of two elements of $L$. Write $B^{\oplus n}$ for the module of $n$-tuples with componentwise operations. Using the polynomial partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative], let $\delta:M\to B^{\oplus n}$ be the $B$-linear map $[f]\mapsto(\pi(\partial f/\partial x_i))_i$. Define the presentation obstruction ideal of $B$ by
$$H_P=\{b\in B:\exists\ h:B^{\oplus n}\to M\text{ additive and }B\text{-linear},\ h\circ\delta=b\operatorname{id}_M\}.$$
Define $H_{B/R}$ to be the intersection of these ideals over all finite polynomial presentations of $B$ over $R$. The index set can be taken to be the finite tuples of elements of $B$ that generate it as an $R$-algebra, with their evaluation maps, and includes the empty tuple when it generates. This is called the Gabber–Ramero obstruction ideal.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NM-6787fc895 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full; there are no new nodes and no tool_uses. Against live it was unsplit before; the delivery makes the statement explicit, adds the quotient-module and polynomial-partial-derivative Mathlib leaves to stmt_deps, adds recorded searches and a split_report, and leaves the blueprint fields untouched. Read Temkin (node URL, pdftotext) §3.2.2, printed p.19: H_F = Ann_F Ext^1(L_{B/A}, J/J^2), and H_{B/A} = H_F·B is the largest ideal of B killing every Ext^1_B(L_{B/A}, N). Checked the presentation form against it: Ext^1(L,N) = coker(Hom(B^n,N) -> Hom(J/J^2,N)) via delta (two-term naive complex, from the triangle). So b kills all of these cokernels iff b*id_M = h∘delta. Hence H_P equals Temkin's H_{B/A} for every presentation, with no Noetherian hypothesis needed. The intersection definition is therefore correct, and the presentation-independence claim correctly stays in the sibling lem-per-gabber-ramero-ideal-calculus. Checked well-definedness of the B-action, of delta (Leibniz gives d(L^2) ⊆ L) and of the ideal property: all elementary from the cited leaves. The index set is a set and is nonempty by finite presentation. Small cases: identity presentation gives H=B; k[x]/(x^2) gives H=(x) in characteristic ≠2 and 0 in characteristic 2, both with V(H) all of Spec B; n=0 gives Ann(I/I^2); the zero ring works. The finitely-presented restriction holds for all four citers. rg -L over the DAG and a grep of the blueprint found no duplicate. The source place's wording 'conormal description' paraphrases Temkin's Ext^1 definition but is mathematically equivalent; not a fault. WANTED: archival copy of Temkin.
